summary: The geometric half of the claim (chromatin moving from the poles to a peripheral ring on the equatorial plane, and what happens when microtubule attachment is perturbed) is testable from Zenodo 5551168, a CC BY 4.0 set of 3D kinetochore tracks in human RPE1 cells from prometaphase to anaphase with nocodazole and Aurora-B-inhibitor conditions, backed by IDR MitoCheck movies (CC0) and the idr0041 mitotic atlas; no archive holds magnetic susceptibility of mitotic chromatin or chromosome motion in an applied field, so the literal diamagnetic reading has no data.
next_step: Pre-register, on the 5551168 tracks, the radial and axial position of kinetochores relative to the inferred spindle axis over time and the equatorial-ring geometry at metaphase, and compare untreated with nocodazole-release conditions; treat the diamagnetic mechanism as the analogy Thompson states it to be.
obstacles_confirmed: Magnetic susceptibility of chromatin during mitosis is not an archived variable.
Equatorial congress is also the prediction of microtubule attachment and congression.
